text: You're halfway to work when you remember you forgot deodorant. Or you're nine hours into a flight. Or you just pulled yesterday's shirt out of a gym bag and immediately regretted it.
For some people, none of that is a problem. Not because they're cleaner. Because a gene called A B C C eleven stopped working.

Fresh sweat is almost odorless. What the bacteria on your skin actually want is one specific molecule, pumped out through the glands under your arm. And A B C C eleven is the pump. Switch it off, and that molecule never reaches the surface.
The bacteria show up to an empty kitchen.
Around eighty to ninety percent of people with East Asian ancestry carry the non-working version.
But here's the part you can check right now. The same switch decides your earwax. Dry and flaky, instead of wet and sticky. That's a clue, not a test.
And nobody has found a clear price for this one. Keep that in mind. It doesn't happen again.
So next time you forget deodorant, run the sniff test before you panic. Some people have been quietly running that experiment their whole lives.
